faqs.question: What is a real estate marketing plan?
faqs.answer: A short written plan, usually for one project or one quarter, that sets out the goal, the buyer, the positioning, the channels, the budget, how enquiries will be handled and how results will be measured.

faqs.question: What are the 7 steps of a real estate marketing plan?
faqs.answer: 1) Set the goal in bookings, 2) define the buyer, 3) write the positioning, 4) choose the channels, 5) set the budget, 6) plan the follow-up, 7) decide what to measure and when to review.

faqs.question: How do I write a marketing plan for a real estate project?
faqs.answer: Start from the sales target and work back to the visits and leads needed, describe the most likely buyer, write one positioning sentence with proof, give each channel a job and a budget, plan the follow-up, and review the numbers weekly.

faqs.question: Which channels should a real estate marketing plan include?
faqs.answer: Usually a mix of Meta ads, Google search ads, property portals, channel partners, hoardings or print, and organic channels like social media and Google Business Profile. With a small budget, run two channels properly rather than many badly.

faqs.question: What should a real estate agent's marketing plan include?
faqs.answer: One or two localities to specialise in, a complete Google Business Profile and RERA number on everything, weekly posts and videos, one paid source to test, same-day follow-up on every enquiry, and a habit of asking for reviews and referrals.

faqs.question: How long should a real estate marketing plan be?
faqs.answer: Two or three pages is enough. A one-page table covering goal, buyer, positioning, offer, channels, creative, follow-up, calendar, measurement and compliance works for most projects.

faqs.question: How often should a real estate marketing plan be reviewed?
faqs.answer: Look at leads, visits and bookings by source every week, and move budget between channels at a monthly review based on cost per site visit and per booking.

faqs.question: Does a real estate marketing plan need to cover RERA?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every ad must carry the project's RERA registration number and the authority's website (plus the QR code in UP), and every claim must match the approved plans and RERA filing.
